readings.title: The Idol-Infested Heart
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Addresses the Stumbling-Block
readings.text: [Ezekiel 14:1] And some of the elders of Yisra’ĕl came to me and sat before me. [2] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [3] <dq>“Son of man, these men have set up their idols in their hearts, and have put <dn>את</dn> the stumbling-block of their crookedness before their face. Should <dn>I</dn> let them inquire of <dn>Me</dn> at all?</dq> [4] <dq>“Therefore speak to them, and you shall say to them, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Everyone of the house of Yisra’ĕl who sets up his idols in his heart, and puts <dn>את</dn> the stumbling-block of his crookedness before his face, and shall come to the prophet – <dn>I</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall answer him who comes, according to his many idols,</dq> [5] <dq>in order to lay hold of <dn>את</dn> the house of Yisra’ĕl by their heart, for they have become estranged from <dn>Me</dn> by their idols, all of them.” ’</dq>

readings.title: The Deceived Prophet
readings.subtitle: Cutting Off the Adversarial Root
readings.text: [6] <dq>“Therefore say to the house of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Repent, and turn back from your idols, and turn back your faces from all your abominations.</dq> [7] <dq>“For anyone of the house of Yisra’ĕl, or of the strangers who sojourn in Yisra’ĕl, who separates himself from <dn>Me</dn> and sets up his idols in his heart and puts <dn>את</dn> the stumbling-block of his crookedness before his face, and shall come to a prophet to inquire of him concerning <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall answer him <dn>Myself</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> face against that man and make him a sign and a proverb, and <dn>I</dn> shall cut <dn>את</dn> him off from the midst of <dn>My</dn> people. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [9] <dq>“And if the prophet is deceived, and shall speak a word, <dn>I</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> have deceived that prophet, and shall stretch out <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> hand against him and destroy him from the midst of <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl.</dq> [10] <dq>“And they shall bear their crookedness, the crookedness of the prophet is the same as the crookedness of the inquirer,</dq> [11] <dq>so that the house of Yisra’ĕl no longer strays from <dn>Me</dn>, nor be made unclean any more with all their transgressions. And they shall be <dn>My</dn> people and <dn>I</dn> be their <dn>Elohim</dn>,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Righteousness of the Three
readings.subtitle: Noah, Daniel, and Job Deliver Only Themselves
readings.text: [Ezekiel 14:12] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came again to me, saying, [13] <dq>“Son of man, when a land sins against <dn>Me</dn> to commit a trespass, and <dn>I</dn> shall stretch out <dn>My</dn> hand against it, and cut off <dn>את</dn> its supply of bread and send scarcity of food on it, and cut off <dn>את</dn> man and beast from it,</dq> [14] <dq>even though these three men, Noaḥ, Dani’ĕl, and Iyoḇ, were in it, they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [15] <dq>“If <dn>I</dn> cause an evil beast to pass through the land, and it shall bereave it, and it shall be a wasteland, so that no man passes through because of the beasts,</dq> [16] <dq>even though these three men were in it, as <dn>I</dn> live,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “they would deliver neither sons nor daughters. They alone would be delivered, but the land be a wasteland.</dq> [17] <dq>“Or if <dn>I</dn> bring a sword on that land, and <dn>I</dn> shall say, ‘Sword, go through the land,’ and <dn>I</dn> shall cut off <dn>את</dn> man and beast from it,</dq> [18] <dq>even though these three men were in its midst, as <dn>I</dn> live,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “they would deliver neither sons nor daughters, for they alone would be delivered.</dq> [19] <dq>“Or if <dn>I</dn> send a pestilence into that land, and <dn>I</dn> shall pour out <dn>My</dn> wrath on it in blood, to cut off from it <dn>את</dn> man and beast,</dq> [20] <dq>even though Noaḥ, Dani’ĕl, and Iyoḇ were in it, as <dn>I</dn> live,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “they would deliver neither son nor daughter. They would deliver their own lives by their righteousness.”</dq>

readings.title: The Four Decrees on Yerushalayim
readings.subtitle: The Remnant Reveals the Purpose of the Wrath
readings.text: [21] <dq>For thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “How much more it shall be when <dn>I</dn> send <dn>My</dn> four evil judgments on Yerushalayim: the sword and scarcity of food and evil beasts and pestilence, to cut off <dn>את</dn> man and beast from it?</dq> [22] <dq>“But see, there shall be left in it a remnant who are brought out, both sons and daughters. See, they are coming out to you, and you shall see their ways and their deeds, and shall be comforted concerning the evil which <dn>I</dn> have brought upon Yerushalayim – all that <dn>I</dn> have brought upon it.</dq> [23] <dq>“And they shall comfort you, when you see their ways and their deeds. And you shall know that it was not for naught that <dn>I</dn> have done whatever <dn>I</dn> did in it,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: The Useless Vine
readings.subtitle: Fuel for the Consuming Fire of Justice
readings.text: [Ezekiel 15:1] Then the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [2] <dq>“Son of man, how is the vine tree better than any tree, the vine branch that has been among the trees of the forest?</dq> [3] <dq>“Is wood taken from it to be made into any work? Do they take a peg from it to hang any vessel on?</dq> [4] <dq>“See, into the fire it shall be given for fuel. Both ends of it the fire shall burn, and its middle shall be scorched. Is it fit for any work?</dq> [5] <dq>“See, when it was intact, it was not made for work, how much less when the fire has burned it and it is scorched shall it still be used for work?</dq> [6] <dq>“Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘As the vine tree among the trees of the forest, which <dn>I</dn> have given to the fire for fuel, so <dn>I</dn> shall give up <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.</dq> [7] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> face against them. They shall go out from fire, but fire consumes them. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when <dn>I</dn> set <dn>My</dn> face against them.</dq> [8] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall make <dn>את</dn> the land a wasteland, because they committed trespass,’ declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>

readings.title: The Blood of the Amorite and Hittite
readings.subtitle: Yerushalayim's Despicable Birth
readings.text: [Ezekiel 16:1] Again the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [2] <dq>“Son of man, make known to Yerushalayim <dn>את</dn> her abominations,</dq> [3] <dq>and say, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to Yerushalayim, “Your origin and your birth are from the land of Kenaʻan. Your father was an Amorite and your mother a Ḥittite.</dq> [4] <dq>“As for your birth, on the day you were born your navel cord was not cut, nor were you washed in water for cleansing, and you were not rubbed with salt at all, nor wrapped in cloth at all.</dq> [5] <dq>“No eye felt sorry for you, to do any of these for you, to have compassion on you. But you were thrown out into the open field, to the loathing of your life on the day you were born.</dq>

readings.title: The Oath of the Covenant
readings.subtitle: Washed and Adorned in Divine Splendour
readings.text: [6] <dq>“Then <dn>I</dn> passed by you and saw you trampled down in your own blood, and <dn>I</dn> said to you in your blood, ‘Live!’ And <dn>I</dn> said to you in your blood, ‘Live!’</dq> [7] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have let you grow like a plant in the field. And you are grown and are great, and you come in the finest ornaments. – breasts were formed, your hair grew, and you were naked and bare.</dq> [8] <dq>“Again <dn>I</dn> passed by you and looked upon you and saw that your time was the time of carnal-love. And <dn>I</dn> spread <dn>My</dn> skirt over you and covered your nakedness. And <dn>I</dn> swore an oath to you and entered into a covenant with you, and you became <dn>Mine</dn>,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> washed you in water, and <dn>I</dn> washed off your blood, and <dn>I</dn> anointed you with oil.</dq> [10] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> dressed you in embroidered work and gave you sandals of leather. And <dn>I</dn> wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with silk.</dq> [11] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> adorned you with ornaments, and <dn>I</dn> put bracelets on your wrists, and a chain on your neck.</dq> [12] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> put a ring on your nose, and earrings in your ears, and a crown of adorning on your head.</dq> [13] <dq>“Thus you were adorned with gold and silver, and your dress was of fine linen, and silk, and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour, and honey, and oil. And you were exceedingly beautiful, and became fit for royalty.</dq> [14] <dq>“And your name went out among the nations because of your loveliness, for it was perfect, by <dn>My</dn> splendour which <dn>I</dn> had put on you,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: The Whorings of the Bride
readings.subtitle: Squandering the Splendour on Dead Images
readings.text: [15] <dq>“But you trusted in your own loveliness, and whored because of your name, and poured out your whorings on everyone passing by who would have it.</dq> [16] <dq>“And you took some of your garments and made multi-coloured high places for yourself, and whored on them – which should not have come about, nor shall it be.</dq> [17] <dq>“And you took <dn>את</dn> your splendid adornments, of <dn>My</dn> gold and <dn>My</dn> silver that <dn>I</dn> gave you, and made for yourself images of a male and whored with them.</dq> [18] <dq>“And you took <dn>את</dn> your embroidered garments and covered them, and you set <dn>My</dn> oil and <dn>My</dn> incense before them.</dq> [19] <dq>“And <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> food which <dn>I</dn> gave you, fine flour and oil and honey which <dn>I</dn> fed you, you set it before them as sweet incense – and so it was,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [20] <dq>“And you took <dn>את</dn> your sons and your daughters, whom you bore to <dn>Me</dn>, and these you slaughtered as food to them. Were your whorings a small matter,</dq> [21] <dq>that you have slain <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> children and gave them up to them by causing them to pass through the fire?</dq> [22] <dq>“And in all your abominations and whorings you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, trampled down in your blood.</dq>

readings.title: Courting the Nations of Ra
readings.subtitle: Mitsrayim, Ashshur, and Kasdima
readings.text: [23] <dq>“Then it came to be after all your evil – ‘Woe, woe to you!’ declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> –</dq> [24] <dq>that you also built an arched place for yourself, and made a high place in every street for yourself.</dq> [25] <dq>“You built your high places at the head of every way, and made your loveliness to be loathed. And you parted your feet to everyone who passed by, and increased your whorings.</dq> [26] <dq>“And you whored with the sons of Mitsrayim, your neighbours, great of flesh. And you increased your whorings to provoke <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [27] <dq>“And see, <dn>I</dn> have stretched out <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> hand against you, and withdrew what is lawfully yours, and gave you up to the desire of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who are ashamed of your wicked way.</dq> [28] <dq>“And you whored with the sons of Ashshur, without being satisfied. And you whored with them and still were not satisfied.</dq> [29] <dq>“And you increased your whorings as far as the land of traders, Kasdima, and even then you were not satisfied.</dq> [30] <dq>“How weak is your heart!” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “seeing you do all this, the deeds of a shameless whore.</dq> [31] <dq>“You built your arched place at the head of every way, and built your high place in every street. Yet you were unlike a whore, you scorned a harlot-fee!</dq> [32] <dq>“The wife who commits adultery who takes strangers instead of her husband!</dq> [33] <dq>“To all whores they give gifts, but you gave gifts to all your lovers, and bribed them to come to you from all around in your whorings.</dq> [34] <dq>“Thus you are different from other women in your whorings, because no one whores after you, and in you giving a harlot-fee, while a harlot-fee was not given to you. Thus you are different.”</dq>

readings.title: The Assembly of Judgment
readings.subtitle: Stripped Bare Before the Lovers
readings.text: [Ezekiel 16:35] Therefore, O whore, hear the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [36] Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Because your copper was poured out and your nakedness uncovered in your whorings with your lovers, and with <dn>את</dn> the idols of your abominations, and because of the blood of your children which you gave to them,</dq> [37] <dq>therefore, see, <dn>I</dn> am gathering <dn>את</dn> all your lovers with whom you took pleasure, all those you loved, with all those you hated. And <dn>I</dn> shall gather them from all around against you and shall uncover your nakedness to them, and they shall see all your nakedness.</dq> [38] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall judge you with judgments of adulteresses and shedders of blood. And <dn>I</dn> shall bring on you the blood of wrath and jealousy.</dq> [39] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> you into their hand, and they shall throw your arched place down, and they shall break down your high places. And they shall strip you of your garments, and they shall take your splendid adornments, and leave you naked and bare.</dq> [40] <dq>“And they shall bring up an assembly against you, and they shall stone you with stones and thrust you through with their swords,</dq> [41] <dq>and burn <dn>את</dn> your houses with fire, and execute <dn>את</dn> judgments on you before the eyes of many women. And <dn>I</dn> shall make you stop whoring, and no longer give harlot-fees.</dq> [42] <dq>“So <dn>I</dn> shall bring <dn>My</dn> wrath to rest upon you, and <dn>My</dn> jealousy shall turn away from you. And <dn>I</dn> shall be calm, and no longer be vexed.</dq> [43] <dq>“Because you did not remember the days of your youth, but troubled <dn>Me</dn> with all this, so see, <dn>I</dn> shall also bring <dn>את</dn> your way on your own head,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. “And shall <dn>I</dn> not do this thought for all your abominations?</dq>

readings.title: Worse than Sedom and Shomeron
readings.subtitle: The Unconcerned Ease and Haughty Abominations
readings.text: [44] <dq>“See, all who use proverbs shall use this proverb against you, ‘Like mother, like daughter!’</dq> [45] <dq>“You are your mother’s daughter, who despises her husband and her children. And you are the sister of your sisters, who despised their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Ḥittite and your father an Amorite.</dq> [46] <dq>“And your elder sister is Shomeron, she and her daughters, who is dwelling to the north of you. And your younger sister, who is dwelling to the south of you, is Seḏom and her daughters.</dq> [47] <dq>“And have you not walked in their ways and did according to their abominations? But in all your ways you soon became more corrupt than they.</dq> [48] <dq>“As <dn>I</dn> live,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “neither your sister Seḏom nor her daughters have done as you and your daughters have done.</dq> [49] <dq>“See, this was the crookedness of your sister Seḏom: She and her daughter had pride, sufficiency of bread, and unconcerned ease. And she did not help the poor and needy.</dq> [50] <dq>“And they were haughty and did abomination before <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> took them away when <dn>I</dn> saw it.</dq> [51] <dq>“And Shomeron did not commit half of your sins, but you have increased your abominations more than they, and by all the abominations which you have done you made your sisters seem righteous!</dq> [52] <dq>“You also, who pleaded for your sisters, bear <dn>את</dn> your own shame, because the sins which you committed were more abominable than theirs. They are more righteous than you. So be ashamed too, and bear <dn>את</dn> your own shame, because you have made your sisters seem righteous.</dq>

readings.title: The Bearing of Shame
readings.subtitle: A Byword in the Days of Pride
readings.text: [53] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall turn back <dn>את</dn> their captivity, the captivity of Seḏom and her daughters, and the captivity of Shomeron and her daughters, and the captivity of your captives with them,</dq> [54] <dq>so that you bear <dn>את</dn> your shame, and shall blush for all that you did when you comforted them,</dq> [55] <dq>“and your sisters, Seḏom and her daughters, return to their former state, and Shomeron and her daughters return to their former state, and you and your daughters return to your former state.</dq> [56] <dq>“Was not your sister Seḏom a byword in your mouth in the days of your pride,</dq> [57] <dq>before your evil was exposed, as the time of the reproach of the daughters of Aram and all who were around her, and of the daughters of the Philistines, who are despising you everywhere?</dq> [58] <dq>“You shall bear <dn>את</dn> your wickedness and <dn>את</dn> your abominations,” declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: The Everlasting Covenant
readings.subtitle: A Pardon to Silence the Shame Forever
readings.text: [59] <dq>For thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “<dn>I</dn> shall deal with you as you have done, in that you have despised <dn>את</dn> the oath by breaking the covenant.</dq> [60] <dq>“But <dn>I</dn> shall remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with you in the days of your youth, and <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> an everlasting covenant with you.</dq> [61] <dq>“And you shall remember <dn>את</dn> your ways and be ashamed, when you receive your older and your younger sisters. And <dn>I</dn> shall give them to you for daughters, though not by your own covenant.</dq> [62] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with you. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [63] <dq>so that you remember. And you shall be ashamed, and never open your mouth any more because of your shame, when <dn>I</dn> pardon you for all you have done,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq>
